title: Redwood forest resilience to wildfires with adaptive management practices
summary: A Cal Poly Humboldt study found that coast redwoods survived extreme 2020 California wildfires well, with most trees repsprouting quickly. However, forest structure—tree density and species composition—significantly influences fire severity and recovery.
takeaways: Study sites: 3 second-growth forests in central California (2020 wildfires)
Sample size: 120+ plots measured for canopy loss, resprouting, death
Key finding: few redwoods died; most dead trees were small
Resprouting: damaged trees produced more new shoots, enabling faster recovery
Management impact: thinning, fuel reduction, species composition affect future severity

title: North American forests show persistent fire deficit despite recent area increases
summary: Analysis shows that despite recent increases in burned area, many North American forest regions remain below their historical fire frequencies—the natural occurrence rates ecosystems depend on.

Implication: mismatch between current fire patterns and long-term ecological baseline
